doc.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03

title: Blues pickers: Blind Lemon, Lead Belly, defining the blues
summary: Albert met Blind Lemon and Lead Belly in east Texas joints and defines the blues as feeling from slavery.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Well, what about. Did you hear any blues pickers up there? No. I don't know. Indianapolis. I mean, real. No. You know, finger picking style. No, no. Yeah.
No, most of that was almost obsolete. Mm-hmm. Oh, sometimes in Texas, I'd run across Blind Lemon.
Mm-hmm. They said lead belly, but his name is Lead belly.
And where would they be playing?
Oh, in joints in, like, Longview, Texas, and all that eastern part of Texas. Yep.
Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. And what's the deal? I just wondered about them because, you know, you never knew whether they were playing in a joint or if they might have been on a stage.
Well, they were old then. They were pretty old then. They weren't doing too much of anything. I think. I think.
Just later years when the revision came, they tried to resurrect them. Oh, whoa. Yeah. It was kind of late then, though.
Hey, you down here at the wheel?

Well, what are the players? The blues is called for feelings. It comes from hope on the slaves. You listen to the words. It's the feelings that the slaves got out of their bodies when they were either blue or happy. That's all the blues is.
